s: What is the IUCN Red List status of the gharial?
x: The gharial is Critically Endangered; the golden langur is Endangered, the one-horned rhino Vulnerable and the Asiatic wild ass Near Threatened.

s: Which of the following is wrongly matched with its IUCN status?
x: The Siberian crane is Critically Endangered, not Endangered.

s: What is the IUCN Red List status of the dhole (Asiatic wild dog)?
x: The dhole and the western hoolock gibbon are both Endangered; Data Deficient is a separate IUCN category.

s: Rollapadu Wildlife Sanctuary in Kurnool district, Andhra Pradesh, is a habitat of which bird?
x: The Great Indian Bustard (Godawan) inhabits the Thar grasslands and Rollapadu WLS; Keibul Lamjao is linked with the Sangai deer.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Gharial?
o: It is associated with the Chambal river system
It is not covered under Project Crocodile
It has been recommended for the Species Recovery Programme
The Supreme Court took suo motu cognisance to protect it
x: The Gharial is a Project Crocodile species.

s: Where is the Irrawaddy dolphin found?
x: The Irrawaddy dolphin is associated with Chilika Lake in Odisha and the Godavari estuary in Andhra Pradesh.

s: Where does the pygmy hog, the world's smallest wild suid, live in alluvial grasslands?
x: The pygmy hog, the only surviving Porcula species, lives in Assam's alluvial grasslands, where captive breeding raised its numbers 32-fold.

s: What is the IUCN Red List status of the tiger?
x: The tiger is Endangered, not Critically Endangered; the Asiatic lion is also Endangered, improved from CR.

s: How many plant taxa did India add to its records in 2025?
x: In 2025 India added 709 animal species (483 new to science) and 353 plant taxa.

s: Which of the following pairs (species – IUCN status) is correctly matched?
x: The wild ass is Near Threatened. The red panda is Endangered, the desert cat Least Concern and the Chinese mountain cat Vulnerable.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Jerdon's Courser — Sri Lankamalleswara Wildlife Sanctuary
x: The Kashmir stag or Hangul is found in Kashmir, particularly Dachigam. Gir in Gujarat is the habitat of the Asiatic lion.

s: What is the IUCN Red List status of the Asiatic lion?
x: The Asiatic lion is Endangered, improved from Critically Endangered.

s: Which of the following pairs (species – IUCN status) is INCORRECTLY matched?
x: The leatherback turtle is Vulnerable, not Critically Endangered.

s: Where is the Sangai deer found?
x: Sangai (EN) lives in Keibul Lamjao, Manipur.

s: Which of the following is the natural habitat of the Great Indian Hornbill?
o: Western Ghats and North-East hill forests
x: The Great Indian Hornbill lives in the Western Ghats and North-East hill forests.

s: From which region were three new Critically Endangered plant species reported in May 2026?
x: The three new CR plants came from AP's Eastern Ghats.

s: In which National Park is the one-horned rhinoceros, listed as Vulnerable, mainly found?
x: The one-horned rhinoceros (Vulnerable) lives mainly in Kaziranga National Park, Assam.

s: The Indian wild ass (Khur), listed as Near Threatened, is found only in which area?
x: The Indian wild ass survives only in the sandy saline Little Rann of Kutch in Gujarat.

s: Which is the only ape found in India?
x: The hoolock gibbon of the North-East is India's only ape; the western hoolock gibbon is Endangered.

s: Besides Chilika Lake, in which estuary of Andhra Pradesh is the Irrawaddy dolphin found?
x: The Irrawaddy dolphin lives in Chilika Lake (Odisha) and the Godavari estuary of Andhra Pradesh.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Irrawaddy dolphin:
1. It is found in Chilika Lake, Odisha.
2. It is found in the Godavari estuary, Andhra Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Irrawaddy dolphin occurs both in Chilika Lake (Odisha) and in the Godavari estuary (AP).

s: How many animal species new to science were added to India's fauna in 2025?
x: In 2025 India added 709 animal species, of which 483 were new to science, and 353 plant taxa.

s: According to the IPBES assessment, about what share of assessed plant and animal species are threatened?
x: IPBES found about 25% of assessed species threatened, with habitat destruction the main driver and extinction rates far above background.

s: The Living Planet Index mainly measures the average change in which of the following?
x: The Living Planet Index, published through WWF's Living Planet assessment, measures the average change in vertebrate populations since 1970.

s: Which of the following is a specialist group functioning under the Species Survival Commission of the IUCN?
x: The Invasive Species Specialist Group (ISSG) functions under the IUCN Species Survival Commission.

s: Where is the headquarters of the IUCN?
x: IUCN, a union of governments and NGOs and not a UN agency, is headquartered at Gland, Switzerland.

s: The Phoenix Species Project (2026), with $200 million funding, aims to recover how many of the world's most threatened species?
x: The Re:wild and Bezos Earth Fund project aims to recover 100 of the most threatened species.

s: Which IUCN tool measures the recovery of a species?
x: The Green Status measures species recovery, whereas the Red List measures extinction risk.

s: In which year was the IUCN Red List, popularly called the 'Barometer of Life', started?
x: The Red List was started in 1964; it measures extinction risk and guides conservation priorities.

s: India's Red List Roadmap, led by the National Biodiversity Authority, aims to assess how many species by 2027?
x: The roadmap aims to assess 70,000 species by 2027.

s: What is the name of the list of endangered species published by the IUCN?
x: The IUCN's list of endangered species is the Red List (Red Data Book), also called the Barometer of Life (APPSC 2025). Brown, White and Black lists are distractors and not the IUCN's list of endangered species.

s: Which of the following pairs (report or database – publisher) is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Living Planet Report – WWF with Zoological Society of London
Global Invasive Species Database – IUCN SSC Invasive Species Specialist Group
Global Assessment on Biodiversity – WWF with Zoological Society of London
x: The Global Assessment on Biodiversity is published by IPBES.

s: In the Red Data Book, what do green pages denote?
x: Green pages mark recovered species; red or pink pages mark endangered and critically endangered ones.

s: In which year was the IUCN founded?
x: IUCN was founded in 1948; the Red List began in 1964 and Green Status in 2021.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the IUCN?
o: Its headquarters is at Gland, Switzerland
Its Species Survival Commission runs specialist groups
x: IUCN is a union of governments and civil-society organisations, not a UN agency.

s: Of the 175,909 species assessed in IUCN Red List 2026-1, about how many are threatened?
x: 49,505 (about 28%) are threatened.

s: Which body published the 2019 Global Assessment on Biodiversity?
x: The Global Assessment is by IPBES, the 'Intergovernmental Panel on Nature', not WWF.

s: Where was the IUCN World Conservation Congress 2025 held?
x: The IUCN World Conservation Congress 2025 was held in Abu Dhabi with the theme 'Our World, Our Future'.

s: Which of the following is one of the 'Evil Quartet' causes of biodiversity loss?
x: The Evil Quartet is habitat loss and fragmentation, over-exploitation, invasive alien species and co-extinctions.

s: Who popularised the HIPPO framework of biodiversity loss?
x: E. O. Wilson popularised HIPPO (Habitat loss, Invasive species, Pollution, human Population, Over-harvesting); co-extinction belongs to the Evil Quartet.

s: Which pair of species is correctly associated with extinction caused by over-exploitation?
o: Steller’s sea cow and passenger pigeon
x: Over-exploitation drove the Steller’s sea cow and the passenger pigeon to extinction.

s: In which framework is co-extinction listed as a cause of biodiversity loss?
o: Both the Evil Quartet and HIPPO
x: Co-extinction belongs to the Evil Quartet; pollution and population belong only to HIPPO.

s:
Consider the following statements about the HIPPO framework:
1. It was popularised by E.O. Wilson.
2. Its two 'P's stand for pollution and human population.
3. It includes co-extinction.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: HIPPO, popularised by Wilson, includes pollution and population; co-extinction is in the Evil Quartet.

s: According to IPBES, which of the following is the main driver of biodiversity loss?
x: IPBES names habitat destruction as the main driver of biodiversity loss; the others are important but rank lower.

s: In India, which factor comes first among the causes of biodiversity loss?
o: Habitat loss from urbanisation, infrastructure, mining and farming
x: In India habitat loss comes first, followed by climate change, invasives, pollution and overexploitation.

s: Which group is especially vulnerable to the effects of habitat fragmentation?
o: Migratory animals and wide-ranging mammals and birds
Sedentary crop plants and soil microbes alone
Only organisms confined to freshwater ponds
x: Habitat fragmentation particularly affects migratory animals and wide-ranging mammals and birds because it disrupts movement and separates populations.

s: Which of the following best explains the edge effect?
o: Edges eliminate all invasive species from a forest patch.
Edges always increase the population of interior-dependent species.
The interior of a fragment becomes darker and cooler as its size decreases.
Patch boundaries experience increased light, wind, heat, predators and weeds, causing the decline of interior species.
x: The edge effect exposes habitat boundaries to greater light, wind, heat, predators and weeds. As fragments shrink, interior species consequently decline.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Removal of invasives with native restocking — disturbance of ecological balance
Draining wetlands — disturbance of ecological balance
x: Removal of invasive species with native restocking restores ecological balance. Clear-felling and draining wetlands disturb it, while afforestation restores it.

s: Tropical rainforest cover has fallen from 14% to about what share of Earth's land surface?
x: Tropical rainforests fell from 14% to 6% of the land surface.

s: Which of the following activities restores ecological balance?
o: Removal of invasives with native restocking
x: Removing invasives with native restocking restores balance; the others disturb it.

s: What is the primary driver of deforestation and habitat loss?
x: Agricultural expansion and urban development are the primary driver of deforestation and habitat loss.

s: In which of the following regions was the ecological damage per invasive alien species found to be higher?
x: Damage per invasive species was found higher in the Global South; removal alone does not necessarily restore landscapes and blanket eradication is debated.

s: Invasive species have contributed to about what share of known animal extinctions since the 17th century?
x: Invasive species have contributed to about 40% of known animal extinctions since the 17th century and threaten about 1 in 10 Red List species.

s: How was Lantana camara brought to India?
x: Lantana came from Central or South America as an ornamental; Parthenium came with wheat, the red-eared slider via the pet trade and mosquitofish for mosquito control.

s: With which imported grain did Parthenium hysterophorus (Congress grass) reach India in the 1950s?
x: Parthenium, from tropical America, came with imported wheat in the 1950s and invades cropland and pasture.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Lantana camara?
o: It is among IUCN's 100 of the World's Worst Invasive Alien Species
It belongs to the family Asteraceae
It occupies about 25% of the forest floor in Amrabad Tiger Reserve
x: Lantana camara belongs to the family Verbenaceae.

s: How does Prosopis juliflora (Seema Chintakaya) mainly affect Rayalaseema?
o: Lowering the groundwater table and raising soil salinity
x: Prosopis drains groundwater in Rayalaseema and raises soil salinity; it has also degraded the Banni grasslands.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Senna spectabilis — North America — invasion of Nilgiri-Bandipur-Wayanad
Giant African Snail — Africa — invasive habitat takeover
Red-eared slider — North America — pet trade
x: Senna spectabilis originated in South America, not North America. The red-eared slider is from North America and spread through the pet trade; mosquitofish came from the United States for mosquito control; the Giant African Snail is from Africa.

s: Which of the following is one of the defining tests for an invasive alien species in India?
x: The three tests are non-native origin, uncontrolled spread and measurable harm; commercial usefulness is not one.

s: Which of the following is listed among invasive fish of concern in India?
x: African catfish, Nile tilapia, red-bellied piranha and alligator gar are listed among invasive fish of concern.

s: In which year was the Plant Quarantine (Regulation of Import into India) Order, requiring pest risk analysis and phytosanitary checks, issued?
x: The Order dates from 2003; DPPQS fumigates uncertified imports with methyl bromide. 1914 is the Destructive Insects and Pests Act.

s: Under which Ministry does the Directorate of Plant Protection, Quarantine and Storage (DPPQS) function?
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
x: DPPQS functions under the Agriculture Ministry, not MoEFCC.

s: Tamil Nadu reported clearing which invasive species from 517 villages in 32 districts?
x: Tamil Nadu reported clearing Prosopis; recovery after removal depends partly on the landscape's prior condition.

s: Where was India's first community-driven programme for removal and restocking against suckermouth catfish, tilapia and African catfish started?
x: The Bombay Natural History Society started India's first community-driven removal and restocking programme at Ujani reservoir in Maharashtra.

s: Under the Wildlife (Protection) Amendment Act, 2022, which provision gives the power to regulate invasive alien species?
x: The Wildlife (Protection) Amendment Act, 2022 empowers the Centre to regulate invasive alien species under Section 62A. The new Schedule IV lists CITES-appendix specimens; it is not the provision that regulates invasives.

s: Which invasive species is called the 'Terror of Bengal'?
x: Water hyacinth, the worst aquatic weed, is called the Terror of Bengal.

s: Which invasive fish is banned in India?
x: The predatory African catfish (Clarias gariepinus) is banned in India.

s: By at least how much does Target 6 of the Kunming-Montreal GBF aim to cut the introduction of invasive alien species by 2030?
x: Target 6 seeks at least a 50% cut by 2030; 30% is the 30x30 figure of Target 3.

s: Which Kunming-Montreal GBF target aims to conserve 30% of land and sea by 2030?
x: Target 3 is 30x30; Target 6 deals with invasive alien species.

s: What does the new Schedule IV of the Wildlife (Protection) Act list after the 2022 amendment?
x: Schedule IV lists CITES-appendix specimens; invasives are regulated under Section 62A.

s: To which family does Lantana camara belong?
x: Lantana is in Verbenaceae, not Asteraceae.

s: To which region is Senna spectabilis, invasive in the Nilgiri-Bandipur-Wayanad landscape, native?
x: Senna spectabilis is from South America, not North America.

s: Water hyacinth, called the worst aquatic weed in the world, is native to which region?
x: Water hyacinth (Eichhornia) comes from the Amazon region of South America.

s: Cashew, introduced into India by the Portuguese, is native to which country?
x: Cashew is native to Brazil; the Portuguese brought it to India about five centuries ago, first to Goa.

s: Which Act aims to stop the entry of crop pests and diseases into India and their inter-state spread?
x: The Destructive Insects and Pests Act, 1914 stops crop pests and diseases from entering India and spreading between States.

s: Which grassland of Gujarat has been degraded by the spread of Prosopis juliflora?
x: Prosopis juliflora (Vilayati Kikar) has degraded the Banni grasslands of Kachchh and reduced their biodiversity.

s: Prosopis juliflora, called Seema Chintakaya in Andhra Pradesh, is native to which region?
o: Mexico, South America and the Caribbean
x: Prosopis juliflora comes from Mexico, South America and the Caribbean; in Rayalaseema it lowers groundwater and raises soil salinity.

s:
Match the following invasive species with the way they came to India:
List-I (Species)
A. Parthenium
B. Lantana camara
C. Red-eared slider
D. Mosquitofish
List-II (How it came)
1. Pet trade
2. Mosquito control
3. With imported wheat
4. As an ornamental
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Parthenium came with imported wheat in the 1950s, Lantana as an ornamental, the red-eared slider through the pet trade and mosquitofish for mosquito control.

s: Which Article of the Convention on Biological Diversity deals with alien species?
x: CBD Article 8(h) asks parties to prevent, control or eradicate alien species that threaten ecosystems.

s: Which of the following is NOT an ecological cause of biodiversity loss?
x: Modern agriculture, loss of genetic variation and habitat destruction contribute to biodiversity loss; loss of appetite is not an ecological cause of extinction.

s: Which combination of traits generally places a species at higher risk of extinction?
o: Large body size, small population, low reproductive rate and narrow specialised niche
Small body size and high adaptability in all habitats
High reproductive rate and wide geographical distribution only
Small body size, large population and broad niche
x: Large body size, small population, low reproductive rate, narrow or specialised niche and endemism are high-risk traits.

s: What is the disappearance of a species that causes the decline or disappearance of species dependent on it called?
x: Co-extinction occurs when the loss of one species causes the decline or loss of dependent species, such as an obligate pollinator or a parasite dependent on a host.

s: What is the present, human-driven wave of extinctions called?
x: The sixth mass extinction is the present human-driven wave; background extinction is slow natural loss at a low steady rate.

s: In which year was the cheetah declared extinct in India?
x: The cheetah was declared extinct in India in 1952 and is regarded as the only large mammal lost in India since Independence.

s: Which of the following was recorded by the Zoological Survey of India as extinct from India?
x: Cheetah, pink-headed duck and mountain quail were recorded as extinct from India; the passenger pigeon was not on this list.

s: When did the fifth mass extinction, which ended the dinosaurs, occur?
x: The end-Cretaceous fifth mass extinction was about 66 million years ago.

s: How many mass extinctions occurred in the past 500 million years before the present one?
x: There were five past mass extinctions; the sixth is happening now.

s: Which of the following is classified as Extinct in the Wild?
x: The Hawaiian crow survives only in captivity; passenger pigeon and Steller's sea cow are Extinct; GIB is CR.

s: The IUCN Red List (2014) recorded how many extinctions in the last 500 years?
x: 784 extinctions in 500 years were recorded in 2014.

s: What is the slow natural loss of species at a low, steady rate called?
x: Background extinction is the slow natural loss of species at a low steady rate, unlike a mass extinction.

s: What is the loss of a high percentage of species in a short geological period called?
x: A mass extinction is the loss of a high percentage of species in a short geological period; Earth has had five.

s: Which of the following is classified as Extinct in the Wild, surviving only in captivity?
x: Père David's deer, like the Hawaiian crow, survives only in captivity, so it is Extinct in the Wild.

s: According to IPBES, how fast are species now going extinct compared with the background rate?
o: Tens to hundreds of times faster
x: IPBES says the present human-driven sixth extinction runs tens to hundreds of times the background rate.

s: The term ‘Threatened’ in the IUCN classification collectively refers to which of the following categories?
x: The term Threatened includes Critically Endangered, Endangered and Vulnerable species.

s: In which IUCN category is a species surviving only in captivity or cultivation, outside its natural range, placed?
x: Extinct in the Wild denotes survival only in captivity or cultivation, outside the natural range; a ten-year gap alone does not make a species Extinct.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: NT stands for Near Threatened, not Not Threatened. DD means Data Deficient, NE means Not Evaluated and VU means Vulnerable.

s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the IUCN criteria designated A to E for assessing extinction risk?
o: Economic value of the species in international trade
x: The criteria include declining population, geographic range, small population size, very small population or restricted distribution, and quantitative extinction-risk analysis. Economic value in international trade is not listed as an A–E criterion.

s:
Arrange the following IUCN categories from highest to lowest risk of extinction:
1. Vulnerable
2. Critically Endangered
3. Near Threatened
4. Endangered
x: The order is CR, EN, VU, NT (then LC).

s: How many categories does the IUCN Red List have?
x: There are nine categories: EX, EW, CR, EN, VU, NT, LC, DD and NE.

s: What does 'NT' stand for in the IUCN Red List?
x: NT means Near Threatened, not 'Not Threatened'.

s: When does the IUCN place a species in the Extinct (EX) category?
o: When it has not been recorded for ten years
When there is no reasonable doubt that the last individual has died, after full surveys
When it survives only in captivity
When its population falls below 50 adults
x: EX needs no reasonable doubt that the last individual has died after full surveys; it is not automatic after ten years unrecorded.

s: In which of the following is Lantana being converted into biochar called 'Black Gold' with Joint Forest Management Committees?
x: In Amrabad Tiger Reserve (Nallamala), Lantana is converted into biochar called 'Black Gold' with Joint Forest Management Committees.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about species habitats in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Red Sanders occurs in the Seshachalam, Veligonda and Nallamala hills
Jerdon's Courser is associated with Sri Lankamalleswara Wildlife Sanctuary, Kadapa
The Slender Loris is found in dry scrub forests
The Golden Gecko is found only in the Western Ghats
x: The Golden Gecko occurs in the Seshachalam Eastern Ghats micro-habitats of Andhra Pradesh.

s: What is the state tree of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Neem is the state tree of Andhra Pradesh, not Red Sanders.

s: Where does Red Sanders, an Endangered tree, occur naturally?
x: Red Sanders (Pterocarpus santalinus) is Endangered and occurs naturally only in Andhra Pradesh's Seshachalam, Veligonda and Nallamala hills.

s: What is the main cause of biodiversity loss in Kolleru Lake?
o: Encroachment by fish and prawn tanks
x: Fish and prawn tanks and unregulated aquaculture have converted wetlands and mangroves into ponds, causing salinity and loss of breeding grounds.

s: Demand from which countries mainly drives illegal logging of Red Sanders in the Seshachalam region?
x: Demand from China and Japan has driven Red Sanders smuggling, illegal logging and associated violence in the Seshachalam region.

s: Why are shrimp farms a biodiversity pressure in Andhra Pradesh?
x: Shrimp farms are associated with replacement of mangroves; bauxite mining, granite quarrying and Red Sanders smuggling are other AP pressures.

s: The Gooty tarantula, a Critically Endangered species listed in CITES Appendix II, is associated with which location?
o: Dachigam National Park of Jammu and Kashmir
x: The Gooty tarantula is associated with the Nandyal forests of Andhra Pradesh and is listed as Critically Endangered and in CITES Appendix II.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Jerdon's courser?
o: It occurs in Sri Lankamalleswara WLS, Kadapa
x: Jerdon's courser is not flightless.

s: The Gooty tarantula is listed under which Schedule of the Wildlife (Protection) Act?
x: It is in WPA Schedule II (Part G) and CITES Appendix II.

s: Which of the following is a major driver of biodiversity loss in the Eastern Ghats of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Bauxite mining is listed as a driver of biodiversity loss in AP's Eastern Ghats.

s: Granite quarrying threatens biodiversity in which hills of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Granite quarrying is a driver of loss in the Seshachalam and Nallamala hills.

s: What is a charismatic species used to rally public support for conservation called?
x: A flagship species is a charismatic species used to generate public support for conservation; the tiger and Asiatic lion are examples.

s: Which one of the following best describes a keystone species?
o: A species whose ecological effect is much greater than would be expected from its population size
A species whose protection automatically protects every species in a country
A species found only in one geographical region
A species selected only for attracting tourism
x: A keystone species has an ecological effect disproportionately larger than its numerical abundance. The tiger as an apex predator and vultures as scavengers illustrate this concept.

s: Protection of which type of species is intended to protect many other species sharing its habitat?
x: An umbrella species is one whose protection indirectly protects many other species. The tiger is an example.

s: Which species appears as a flagship, keystone and umbrella species?
x: The tiger is a flagship, keystone (apex predator) and umbrella species.

s: Which of the following is the One Health approach particularly relevant to addressing?
o: Zoonotic spillover arising from habitat disruption and wildlife trade
Replacement of all wildlife with domestic species
Only the restoration of urban roads
x: Zoonotic spillover may increase through habitat disruption and wildlife trade. The One Health approach recognises the interconnected health of humans, animals and ecosystems.

s:
Assertion (A): Climate change has no effect on species migration.
Reason (R): Rising temperatures can shift species ranges.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: A is false: warming can disrupt migration and alter ranges. R is true; warming can also raise extinction risk in hotspots and help alien plants reach the Arctic.

s: By disrupting which of the following does biodiversity loss mainly reduce the food security of resource-dependent communities?
o: Pollination, nutrient cycling and water and soil services
x: Loss of pollination, nutrient cycling and water and soil services undermines food security.

s:
Consider the following statements about climate change as a driver of biodiversity loss:
1. Warming causes coral bleaching and ocean acidification.
2. A warming Arctic is opening up to alien plants.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are effects of climate change on biodiversity.

s: In which zone of a Biosphere Reserve are settlements allowed?
x: Settlements may exist in the transition zone; National Parks allow no rights or grazing at all.

s: Which protected-area category is zoned into core, buffer and transition areas?
x: A Biosphere Reserve has core, buffer and transition zones; National Parks are clearly demarcated, and sanctuary boundaries are not strictly specified.

s: Which Biosphere Reserve harbours the highest number of animal species among Indian Biosphere Reserves, with 2,626 species?
x: The Sundarbans Biosphere Reserve harbours the highest number of animal species among Indian Biosphere Reserves, reported as 2,626.

s: The Citrus Gene Sanctuary in Nokrek Biosphere Reserve is an in-situ conservation site for which of the following?
x: The Citrus Gene Sanctuary in Nokrek Biosphere Reserve, Garo Hills, Meghalaya, conserves crop wild relatives in situ.

s: Manas Biosphere Reserve is linked with which protected area?
x: Manas Biosphere Reserve is linked with the Manas Wildlife Sanctuary, not with Sundarbans National Park.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the zonation of a biosphere reserve?
o: The core zone is legally protected, usually as a National Park or sanctuary
The transition zone permits settlements, agriculture, forestry and tourism
The buffer zone is the outer interface where settlements, farming and tourism are concentrated
The buffer zone allows regulated activities such as research, education and training
x: The buffer zone surrounds the core and allows only regulated activities; settlements, farming and tourism belong to the transition zone, the outer interface.

s: Which of the following correctly describes the funding pattern for biosphere reserves?
o: 100 per cent central funding for all biosphere reserves
60:40 for the North-Eastern States, and 90:10 for all other States
90:10 for the North-Eastern and three Himalayan States, and 60:40 for other States
x: The funding pattern is 90:10 for the North-Eastern States and three Himalayan States, and 60:40 for other States.

s: Which of the following is NOT a criterion associated with UNESCO's Biosphere Reserve framework?
o: A management authority involving local or tribal communities
Viable populations representing all trophic levels in the core
An effectively protected and minimally disturbed core
Compulsory transfer of land ownership to UNESCO
x: UNESCO's criteria include a protected core, viable populations across trophic levels and participatory management. Transfer of land ownership to UNESCO is not a criterion.

s: Which organisation launched the Man and the Biosphere (MAB) Programme in 1971, under which Biosphere Reserves are designated?
x: The MAB Programme, launched in 1971, is a UNESCO programme, and Biosphere Reserves were started by UNESCO, not IUCN. IUCN deals with the Red List and PA categories, UNEP with the environment programme and WDPA (via UNEP-WCMC), and WWF is an NGO.

s: Which Biosphere Reserve, including Lahaul-Spiti, is India's first high-altitude cold desert site in UNESCO's World Network?
x: The Cold Desert Biosphere Reserve in Lahaul-Spiti (Pin Valley NP, Kibber WLS, Chandratal) is India's first high-altitude cold desert site in the WNBR.

s: Of India's 18 Biosphere Reserves, how many are included in UNESCO's World Network of Biosphere Reserves?
x: 13 of India's 18 Biosphere Reserves are in UNESCO's World Network of Biosphere Reserves.

s: Which Indian Biosphere Reserve was included in UNESCO's World Network of Biosphere Reserves in 2016?
x: Agasthyamalai entered the World Network in 2016. Seshachalam, Manas and Dibru-Saikhowa are among the five not yet included.

s: Which was the first Biosphere Reserve established in India?
x: Nilgiri was India’s first Biosphere Reserve, designated in 1986.

s: Which is the largest Biosphere Reserve in India by area?
x: The Great Rann of Kutch in Gujarat is the largest Indian Biosphere Reserve by area.

s: The Achanakmar-Amarkantak Biosphere Reserve covers which States?
x: Achanakmar-Amarkantak covers Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh; Agasthyamalai covers Kerala and Tamil Nadu.

s: Seshachalam Hills Biosphere Reserve is located in which state?
x: Seshachalam Hills Biosphere Reserve (2010) is in Andhra Pradesh, in the Tirupati hills.

s: In which State is the Dihang-Dibang Biosphere Reserve located?
x: Dihang-Dibang is in Arunachal Pradesh; Cold Desert is the biosphere reserve in Himachal Pradesh.

s: Which of the following Biosphere Reserve – year pairs is correctly matched?
x: Cold Desert dates from 2009. Achanakmar–Amarkantak dates from 2005 and Seshachalam Hills from 2010.

s: In which year was the Seshachalam Biosphere Reserve, spanning the Tirupati and Kurnool Forest Circles, notified?
x: Seshachalam Biosphere Reserve was notified in 2010 and spans the Tirupati and Kurnool Circles.

s: In which year was the Kachchh Biosphere Reserve in Gujarat established?
x: Kachchh Biosphere Reserve dates from 2008, not 2009; Panna is 2011 and Pachmarhi 1999.

s: In which year was Nilgiri, India's first biosphere reserve, established?
x: Nilgiri dates from 1986; Nanda Devi came in 1988, Gulf of Mannar in 1989 and Similipal in 1994.

s: In India, which body recommends sites for biosphere reserves?
x: The IN-MAB Committee under MoEF&CC recommends sites, while the States prepare Management Action Plans.

s: What is the name of the 1995 strategy that added social, cultural and economic needs to Biosphere Reserve criteria?
x: The Seville Strategy of 1995 added social, cultural and economic needs and community participation to Biosphere Reserve criteria.

s: In which year was the Agasthyamalai Biosphere Reserve, home of the Kani tribe, established?
x: Agasthyamalai Biosphere Reserve, spanning Tamil Nadu and Kerala, was established in 2001.

s: In which State is the Khangchendzonga Biosphere Reserve located?
x: Khangchendzonga is in Sikkim; Nanda Devi is in Uttarakhand.

s: Which is the only Indian Biosphere Reserve spread over three States?
x: Nilgiri (Tamil Nadu-Kerala-Karnataka) is the only three-State Biosphere Reserve; Agasthyamalai and Achanakmar-Amarkantak span two States.

s: Where was the 37th MAB-ICC session, which added the Cold Desert Biosphere Reserve to UNESCO's World Network, held?
x: Cold Desert became India's 13th WNBR site at the 37th MAB-ICC, Hangzhou, in September 2025.

s: Which of the following Biosphere Reserves of India is NOT included in UNESCO's World Network of Biosphere Reserves?
x: Seshachalam (AP) is one of five Indian Biosphere Reserves outside the World Network; Nilgiri, Similipal and Panna are included.

s: Which of the following pairs of Biosphere Reserves are both outside UNESCO's World Network of Biosphere Reserves?
x: Manas, Dibru-Saikhowa, Dehang-Dibang, Great Rann of Kutch and Seshachalam are not in the World Network; the others are.

s: Which is the largest UNESCO-approved biosphere reserve of India?
x: Gulf of Mannar (about 10,500 sq km) is the largest Indian BR in UNESCO's network; Kachchh is larger but not in it.

s: In which year was the Great Nicobar Biosphere Reserve included in UNESCO's World Network of Biosphere Reserves?
x: Great Nicobar BR (A&N Islands, 1989) joined UNESCO's World Network in 2013.

s: The Great Indian Bustard, known as Godawan, is the State bird of which State?
x: The Godawan is Rajasthan's State bird; its population is estimated at fewer than 150.

s: With reference to Nanda Devi, which one of the following is a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
o: Nanda Devi Biosphere Reserve as a whole
Nanda Devi and Valley of Flowers National Parks
Nanda Devi Wildlife Sanctuary in Madhya Pradesh
x: The World Heritage Site is Nanda Devi and Valley of Flowers National Parks; the Biosphere Reserve itself is not the WHS (UKPSC 2025 key treated 'Nanda Devi BR is a WHS' as wrong). There is no Nanda Devi tiger reserve, and Nanda Devi is in Uttarakhand, not MP.

s: Silent Valley National Park, a tropical evergreen forest, is located in which State?
x: Silent Valley National Park is in Palakkad district of Kerala, not Tamil Nadu.

s: TRAFFIC, the wildlife-trade monitoring network, is a joint alliance of which organisations?
x: TRAFFIC is a joint WWF-IUCN network; BirdLife International identifies Important Bird and Biodiversity Areas.

s: With which organisation is the Red List of threatened species associated?
x: IUCN runs the Red List; GEF funds environmental work and FAO covers food, farming and forests.

s: In which year was TRAFFIC, the WWF-IUCN alliance that monitors wildlife trade, established?
x: TRAFFIC was set up in 1976 to monitor trade in plants and animals.

s: On the phumdis of which lake does Keibul Lamjao, the world's only floating National Park, float?
x: Keibul Lamjao in Manipur floats on the phumdis of Loktak Lake and is home of the Sangai deer.

s: Which is the Indian partner of BirdLife International for Important Bird and Biodiversity Areas?
x: BirdLife International designates IBAs, and its Indian partner is the BNHS, not WII.

s: In which district of Uttarakhand is the Valley of Flowers National Park located?
x: The Valley of Flowers National Park (87 sq km) is in Chamoli district of Uttarakhand and is a World Heritage Site with Nanda Devi NP.

s: Anamalai Tiger Reserve is associated with which of the following conservation firsts?
x: Anamalai is associated with India's first Hornbill Conservation Centre.

s: Palk Bay, covering about 448 square kilometres, has been designated as India's first what?
o: Important Coastal and Marine Biodiversity Area
x: Palk Bay, covering about 448 square kilometres, is India's first Dugong Conservation Reserve.

s: Who names Hope Spots, the ocean areas critical to ocean health?
o: UNESCO's Man and the Biosphere Programme
Mission Blue, associated with Sylvia Earle
x: Hope Spots are ocean sites named by Mission Blue, an initiative associated with marine scientist Sylvia Earle.

s: In which year were Andaman and Nicobar and Lakshadweep named India's first Hope Spots?
x: Mission Blue, with IUCN, named Andaman and Nicobar and Lakshadweep India's first Hope Spots in 2013.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. India has identified 106 Important Coastal and Marine Biodiversity Areas.
2. Naupada, an Important Coastal and Marine Biodiversity Area, is in Srikakulam district of Andhra Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: India has 106 Important Coastal and Marine Biodiversity Areas, and Naupada in Srikakulam (AP) is one of them.

s: In which district of Andhra Pradesh is the Naupada Important Coastal and Marine Biodiversity Area located?
x: Naupada, an Important Coastal and Marine Biodiversity Area, lies in Srikakulam district of AP.

s: Where is the National Centre for Marine Biodiversity located?
x: The National Centre for Marine Biodiversity is at Jamnagar, Gujarat.

s: Where was India's first Marine National Park set up?
x: India's first Marine National Park and sanctuary is in the Gulf of Kachchh near Jamnagar, Gujarat.

s: Coral restoration at Vaan Island is taking place in which marine national park?
x: Vaan Island lies in the Gulf of Mannar Marine NP (Tamil Nadu, 1986), where coral restoration was done in June 2026.

s: Which of the following are field gene banks most suitable for conserving?
o: vegetatively propagated crops and crops with recalcitrant seeds
only orthodox seeds kept in dry cold storage
x: Field gene banks maintain living collections, especially of vegetatively propagated crops and crops with recalcitrant seeds, such as mango, coconut and banana.

s: Which of the following pairs of facility and location is wrongly matched?
o: International Rice Genebank – Los Baños, Philippines
x: The Millennium Seed Bank is at Wakehurst in the United Kingdom; Chang La hosts the high-altitude seed vault.

s: LaCONES at Hyderabad is best described as which one of the following?
o: A national authority for licensing zoos
India’s frozen zoo using assisted reproduction and DNA banking
India’s first botanical garden for medicinal plants
A wildlife census office under UNESCO
x: LaCONES, the Laboratory for the Conservation of Endangered Species, is associated with CSIR-CCMB at Hyderabad and functions as India’s frozen zoo using assisted reproduction and DNA banking.

s: Which facility, built inside a mountain in permafrost, serves as a global safety duplicate of seed collections?
x: The Svalbard Global Seed Vault lies inside a mountain in permafrost and holds duplicate seed samples, including India's.

s: Which of the following can be preserved by cryopreservation?
o: Gametes, embryos, seeds, pollen, tissues and DNA
x: Cryopreservation applies to gametes, embryos, seeds, pollen, disease-free meristems, tissues and DNA.

s: What is the capacity of the second National Gene Bank announced in the Union Budget 2025-26?
x: The second National Gene Bank will hold 10 lakh germplasm lines and act as a safety duplicate.

s: What is the stated capacity of the Svalbard Global Seed Vault?
x: The Svalbard Global Seed Vault in Norway can hold about 4.5 million seed samples. That figure is its capacity, not what it actually holds; the trap is reading 'over 4 million varieties' as current holdings. The 10 lakh figure is the capacity of India's second National Gene Bank.

s: NBFGR is the national bureau for the genetic resources of what?
x: NBFGR deals with fish; NBAGR handles livestock, NBPGR plants and NBAIM microorganisms.

s: Where is India's National Gene Bank, run by ICAR-NBPGR for plant and crop genetic resources, located?
x: The National Gene Bank of ICAR-NBPGR is at New Delhi (set up 1996, about 4.7 lakh accessions). Karnal hosts NBAGR (animal genetic resources) and Lucknow hosts NBFGR (fish); Hyderabad has LaCONES, the frozen zoo.

s: Cryopreservation generally uses which medium and temperature?
x: Cryopreservation is generally carried out in liquid nitrogen at −196°C, which halts metabolic activity and preserves viability for very long periods.

s: Which of the following ICAR bureau – location pairs is correctly matched?
x: NBAIM (microorganisms) is at Mau; NBAGR is at Karnal, NBFGR at Lucknow and NBPGR at New Delhi.

s: NBAGR, the ICAR bureau at Karnal, conserves the genetic resources of what?
x: NBAGR at Karnal holds livestock genetic resources; plants are with NBPGR, fish with NBFGR, microbes with NBAIM.

s: Where is a field gene bank of the National Botanical Research Institute located?
x: NBRI's Banthara station holds a field gene bank of living plant collections.

s: In which country is the Millennium Seed Bank, the largest store of wild plant seeds, located?
x: The Millennium Seed Bank of Kew is at Wakehurst, UK; Svalbard is in Norway and the rice genebank in the Philippines.

s: Along with NBPGR, which body runs the seed vault at Chang La in Ladakh?
x: The Chang La seed vault (~17,300 ft) is run by DRDO's DIHAR with NBPGR and uses the natural cold.

s: LaCONES, India's frozen zoo at Hyderabad, bred which animal with Nehru Zoological Park for reintroduction?
x: LaCONES (CSIR-CCMB) bred the Indian mouse deer with Nehru Zoo for reintroduction.

s: Under which conditions do seeds remain viable for the longest time in storage?
x: Low moisture and low temperature slow respiration and fungal growth, so seeds keep longest when cool and dry.

s: At about what temperature does the Svalbard Global Seed Vault store seeds?
x: Svalbard stores seeds at about -18°C in permafrost; -196°C is the liquid-nitrogen temperature used in cryopreservation.

s: Why is in-situ conservation generally considered the most effective method?
o: Eliminates the need for protected areas
Can conserve only genetic material and not living species
Keeps species interacting with their environment
Stores all organisms in artificial conditions
x: In-situ conservation maintains species within their natural environment, allowing continued ecological interactions and processes.

s: Which of the following is an appropriate example of captive breeding as an ex-situ conservation intervention?
o: Protecting a wetland as an OECM
Declaring a sacred grove as a Community Reserve
Breeding Gangetic gharials and releasing them into suitable rivers
Regulating tourism in a National Park
x: Captive breeding is suitable when a species' habitat has been permanently lost; bred animals may subsequently be released, as in the reintroduction of Gangetic gharials in several states.

s: Which one of the following correctly compares in-situ and ex-situ conservation?
o: In-situ conserves only genes, whereas ex-situ conserves complete ecosystems in nature.
In-situ protects the whole ecosystem, whereas ex-situ primarily conserves the species or its genes outside the natural habitat.
Ex-situ is used only for landscapes, whereas in-situ is used only for laboratories.
Both methods necessarily conserve the whole ecosystem in its original location.
x: In-situ conservation protects species along with their ecological setting, while ex-situ conservation focuses mainly on species or genetic material outside the natural habitat.

s: Sacred groves are an example of which type of conservation?
x: Sacred groves protect species where they live, so they are in-situ conservation.

s: Which of the following is an example of in-situ conservation?
x: A national park protects species in their habitat; botanical gardens, zoos and gene banks are ex-situ.

s: Which of the following is an example of ex-situ conservation?
x: A cryobank stores seeds, sperm or tissue frozen outside the habitat, so it is ex-situ. Sanctuaries, biosphere reserves and national parks are in-situ.

s: Why is meristem culture particularly useful in ex-situ conservation?
o: Conversion of a Community Reserve into a National Park
Protection of animals in a wildlife sanctuary
Natural pollination in a protected forest
x: Meristem culture is a tissue-culture technique used for virus-free propagation of plants.

s: Which one of the following is NOT a limitation of ex-situ conservation?
o: Maintaining captive populations can be resource-intensive.
It may support education, research and reintroduction.
It cannot by itself save the entire ecosystem.
It requires considerable space and money.
x: Education, research and reintroduction are values of ex-situ conservation, not limitations. Space and financial requirements, as well as inability to save the whole ecosystem, are limitations.

s: Who first used the term 'biological diversity'?
x: Raymond F. Dasmann first used the term 'biological diversity' in 1968.

s: Which one of the following is NOT a protected area category under the Wildlife (Protection) Act framework?
x: The four protected area categories are National Park, Wildlife Sanctuary, Conservation Reserve and Community Reserve. Biosphere Reserve is not included in this four-category classification.

s: Which of the following describes an Eco-sensitive Zone (ESZ) around a National Park or Wildlife Sanctuary?
o: shock absorber and transition zone between high protection and areas where some development may be allowed
strictly urbanised buffer for industrial development
zone where all forms of human activity are permanently prohibited
separate category of biosphere reserve administered by UNESCO
x: An ESZ functions as a shock absorber around a protected area, providing a transition from high protection to areas where regulated development may be permitted.

s: From which body do projects affecting wildlife in or around protected areas require clearance?
o: Standing Committee of the National Board for Wildlife
x: Projects affecting wildlife require clearance from the Standing Committee of the National Board for Wildlife (NBWL).

s: In which of the following may grazing of livestock be regulated by the Chief Wildlife Warden?
o: Both National Parks and Wildlife Sanctuaries
x: Grazing is fully banned in National Parks; it may be regulated only in Wildlife Sanctuaries.

s: Who declares a Community Reserve?
x: The State Government declares a Community Reserve; land already under a national park, sanctuary or conservation reserve cannot become one.

s: What is the purpose of a Community Reserve?
o: Fauna and flora as well as traditional and cultural values
x: A community reserve conserves plants and animals as well as traditional and cultural values.

s: Which one of the following is NOT a feature of an OECM?
o: Recognition automatically changes land ownership and confers new legal authority.
It is demarcated and has inclusive governance.
It is outside the formal protected-area network.
x: Recognition of an OECM is outcome-based and does not change land ownership or confer new legal, financial or management authority. The other three are among its criteria.

s: As of 2026, India's protected-area network comprised how many protected areas?
x: The network grew from 981 protected areas in 2020 to 1,134 in 2026, covering 5.32% of India's area.

s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Conservation Reserve – State-owned land near or linking protected areas
Community Reserve – private or community land voluntarily offered for conservation
National Park – private or community land voluntarily offered for conservation
Tiger Reserve – notified under the NTCA chapter
x: Voluntarily offered private or community land forms a Community Reserve; a National Park allows no rights or grazing, and altering its boundary needs NBWL recommendation.

s: The Keshopur-Chhamb community reserve is located in which State?
x: Keshopur-Chhamb, India's first community reserve, is in Punjab, not Rajasthan; community reserves came with the 2002 WPA amendment.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about protected areas in India?
o: A Biosphere Reserve is associated with UNESCO's Man and the Biosphere Programme
Biosphere Reserve recognition does not by itself change the legal status or ownership of land
National Parks are established under the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972 through State notification
Wildlife Sanctuaries are established only through UNESCO notification
x: Wildlife Sanctuaries are notified by the State under the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972; UNESCO does not notify them.

s: On whose recommendation can the boundary of a National Park be altered by a resolution of the State Legislature?
x: Under the WPA 1972, a National Park's boundary is altered only by a State Legislature resolution on NBWL recommendation.

s:
Consider the following statements about protected-area categories:
1. A Conservation Reserve is declared on government land.
2. A Community Reserve is declared on private or community land.
3. Amchang is notified as a community reserve.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Conservation reserves are on government land and community reserves on private/community land; Amchang is a wildlife sanctuary, not a community reserve.

s: As of 2026, protected areas cover about what share of India's geographical area?
x: India's 1,134 protected areas cover only about 5.32% of its area (Aug 2026).

s: Which one of the following sets contains only activities classified as REGULATED in an Eco-sensitive Zone?
o: Tree felling, hotels and resorts, road widening
Ongoing agriculture, organic farming, rainwater harvesting
Major hydro projects, commercial mining, ongoing agriculture
x: Tree felling, hotels and resorts, and road widening are regulated activities. Commercial mining and major hydro projects are prohibited, while ongoing agriculture, organic farming and rainwater harvesting are permitted.

s:
Consider the following statements about Eco-sensitive Zones:
1. They are notified under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
2. They are notified under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: ESZs are notified under the EP Act, 1986 (Section 3 read with Rule 5 of the EP Rules), not under the WPA, 1972.

s: Under the Supreme Court's order, no mining is allowed within what distance of any National Park or Wildlife Sanctuary?
x: The Supreme Court barred mining within 1 km of any NP/WLS, unless a larger notified ESZ prevails; 10 km is the MoEF 2011 guideline.

s: Which of the following activities is PROHIBITED in an Eco-sensitive Zone?
x: Commercial mining is prohibited in an ESZ; road widening is regulated, and organic farming and rainwater harvesting are permitted.

s: What is an Other Effective Area-based Conservation Measure (OECM)?
o: A temporary area protected only during a breeding season
An ex-situ facility for storing genetic material
An area outside the formal protected-area network that delivers long-term in-situ conservation outcomes
A formally notified National Park with the highest legal protection
x: An OECM is outside the formal protected-area network but delivers long-term in-situ conservation outcomes and is recognised on the basis of its results.

s: Which organisation maintains the World Database on Protected Areas (WDPA) in collaboration with IUCN?
x: The WDPA is run by UNEP-WCMC, based in Cambridge, in collaboration with IUCN, and tracks progress towards the 30x30 target.

s: In 2014, what proportion of the world's land area and coastal-marine area was covered by protected areas, respectively?
x: In 2014, protected areas covered 15.2% of global land and 8.4% of coastal and marine areas.

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the present trend in global ocean protection?
o: Nearly 10% of the ocean is protected, but only about 3% is fully or highly protected.
Nearly 30% of the ocean is protected, including 15% that is fully protected.
Only 1.66% of the ocean is protected, while nearly 10% is fully protected.
The proportion of protected ocean area has declined since 2014.
x: Nearly 10% of the ocean is protected, but only about 3% is fully or highly protected; merely 1.66% of the high seas is protected.

s: What does the '30x30' target of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework refer to?
o: Generating 30% of electricity from renewable sources by 2030
Protecting 30% of the world's land and oceans by 2030
Reducing greenhouse gas emissions by 30% from 2030 levels
Restoring 30 million hectares of degraded land by 2030
x: 30x30 (Target 3 of the KMGBF, CBD COP-15, 2022) aims to protect 30% of land and oceans by 2030. It is not a renewable-energy target (a PYQ trap), nor an emissions-cut or land-restoration target.

s: Which of the following best explains the role of Other Effective Area-Based Conservation Measures (OECMs) in relation to the 30x30 conservation objective?
o: They are restricted to marine areas and cannot include community-managed landscapes.
They include only areas inside National Parks and Wildlife Sanctuaries.
They recognise effective conservation areas outside conventional protected areas and can help meet the 30x30 objective.
They replace all Biosphere Reserves recognised under UNESCO's MAB Programme.
x: OECMs can cover effectively conserved areas outside reserve forests, National Parks and Wildlife Sanctuaries, including sacred groves, greenbelts and wetlands, and thereby support the 30x30 objective.

s: Which was India's first OECM, recognised in 2022?
o: Gulf of Mannar Biosphere Reserve, Tamil Nadu
Great Himalayan National Park, Himachal Pradesh
x: Aravalli Biodiversity Park in Gurugram, a restored mining site, was recognised as India's first OECM in 2022.

s: Up to what distance around a protected area do MoEF's 2011 guidelines allow an Eco-sensitive Zone?
x: The 2011 guidelines allow an ESZ of up to 10 km around a protected area.

s: In June 2022, what minimum eco-sensitive zone around protected areas did the Supreme Court make mandatory?
x: The Supreme Court mandated a minimum 1 km ESZ in June 2022; the 2002–16 Wildlife Action Plan had suggested 10 km.

s: Under which Act does the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change notify Eco-sensitive Zones?
x: ESZs are notified by MoEF&CC under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, and not under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.

s: Which Wildlife Action Plan had suggested a 10 km Eco-sensitive Zone around protected areas?
x: The Wildlife Action Plan 2002-16 suggested 10 km; the Supreme Court (June 2022) made a 1 km minimum mandatory.

s: Where is the National Wildlife Genetic Resource Bank, storing DNA, tissues, gametes and embryos of wild animals, located?
x: The bank is at Nehru Zoological Park and stores DNA, tissues, gametes and embryos of endangered wild animals.

s: In which zoo are the two giant tortoises gifted by Seychelles in 2018 kept?
x: Seychelles gifted two giant tortoises in 2018 to Nehru Zoological Park, Hyderabad, which also has the National Wildlife Genetic Resource Bank.

s: The Jatayu Conservation Breeding Centre at Pinjore is associated with the conservation of which birds?
x: Jatayu Conservation Breeding Centre at Pinjore breeds vultures; the GIB is bred at Sam and Ramdevra, the red panda at Padmaja Naidu Himalayan Zoological Park.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden — Shibpur, Howrah
National Botanical Garden of CSIR-NBRI — Darjeeling
x: The Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden, known for the Great Banyan and associated with the Botanical Survey of India, is at Shibpur in Howrah, West Bengal.

s: The 2024 Supreme Court order relating to the habitat of the Great Indian Bustard mandated which measure?
o: Conversion of the habitat into a marine reserve
x: The 2024 Supreme Court order mandated underground power lines in the Great Indian Bustard’s habitat to reduce threats to the species.

s: Where is the Lloyd Botanical Garden located?
x: Lloyd Botanical Garden is at Darjeeling; Ooty has the Government Botanical Garden and Lucknow the National Botanical Garden of CSIR-NBRI.

s: The National Medicinal Plants Board (NMPB), established in 2000, functions under which Ministry?
o: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
x: The NMPB was established in 2000 under the Ministry of AYUSH and promotes the cultivation and conservation of medicinal plants.

s:
Assertion (A): The Central Zoo Authority (CZA) is a statutory body.
Reason (R): The CZA was provided for by the 1991 amendment to the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: CZA is statutory precisely because the 1991 amendment to the WPA, 1972 provided for it.

s: Where is conservation breeding of the red panda carried out?
x: Red panda breeding is at Padmaja Naidu Zoo, Darjeeling; Pinjore breeds vultures and Sam the Great Indian Bustard.

s: In which year was the Central Zoo Authority set up?
x: The CZA was provided for by the 1991 WPA amendment and set up in 1992.

s: Under the Biological Diversity Rules, 2024, what is the approval period for IPR-related matters?
x: The 2024 Rules mention 180 days for IPR-related matters and 90 days generally.

s: What is the aim of CSIR's Phyto-Pharma Plant Mission?
o: Set up zoos for medicinal animals
Ban the export of all medicinal plants
Cultivate threatened endemic medicinal plants and find new plant-based drugs
x: CSIR's Phyto-Pharma Plant Mission cultivates threatened endemic medicinal plants and develops new plant drugs.

s: Where are the conservation breeding centres of the Great Indian Bustard located?
x: GIB conservation breeding centres are at Sam and Ramdevra in Jaisalmer, Rajasthan.

s: On what basis are sacred groves mainly preserved by communities?
o: religious beliefs, with trees and wildlife being venerated
x: Sacred groves are forest patches preserved by communities on religious grounds, where trees and wildlife are traditionally venerated.

s: Which of the following sacred grove – State pairs is correctly matched?
x: Devrai (Devrahati) is the Maharashtra name for sacred groves. Kavu is from Kerala, Orans from Rajasthan and Sarna from Jharkhand.

s: In which year did the Khejarli incident, linked to the Bishnoi tradition of protecting khejri trees, take place?
x: In 1730 at Khejarli, Amrita Devi and 363 Bishnois died protecting khejri trees from the Jodhpur king's men.

s: Which of the following sacred grove – State pairs is wrongly matched?
x: Orans are sacred groves of Rajasthan; Meghalaya's are Law Kyntang or Law Lyngdoh.

s: In which State is Law Kyntang the local name for sacred groves?
x: Law Kyntang (Law Lyngdoh) are Meghalaya's sacred groves; Manipur's are Umanglai and Karnataka's Devarakadu.

s: How many Bishnois died with Amrita Devi at Khejarli in 1730 protecting khejri trees?
x: Amrita Devi and 363 Bishnois died at Khejarli in 1730 protecting khejri trees from the Jodhpur king's men.

s: Jerdon's Courser is associated with which protected area of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Jerdon's Courser is associated with Sri Lankamalleswara Wildlife Sanctuary; Seshachalam is known for Red Sanders, Cycas beddomei and the Golden Gecko.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: Rollapadu is associated with the Great Indian Bustard, not the Golden Gecko. The Golden Gecko is associated with Seshachalam.

s: Coringa Wildlife Sanctuary protects the mangroves of which estuary?
x: Coringa protects Godavari-estuary mangroves; Krishna Wildlife Sanctuary protects Krishna-estuary mangroves.

s: Hope Island near Coringa was reported to face a threat from which proposed project?
x: Hope Island near Coringa was reported to be threatened by a satellite launch facility.

s: Which of the following sanctuary – species pairs is correctly matched?
x: Rollapadu (Kurnool) protects the Great Indian Bustard; Sri Lankamalleswara is known for Jerdon's Courser and Koundinya for elephants.

s: Where is India's largest pelicanry of spot-billed pelicans?
x: Nelapattu (1976), near Pulicat, is India's largest spot-billed pelican pelicanry.

s:
Arrange the following AP sanctuaries in chronological order of notification:
1. Rollapadu
2. Coringa
3. Krishna
4. Nelapattu
x: Nelapattu 1976, Coringa 1978, Rollapadu 1988 and Krishna 1989.

s: In which year was the Coringa Wildlife Sanctuary notified?
x: Coringa dates from 1978; Nelapattu is 1976, Rollapadu 1988 and Krishna 1989.

s: Which of the following water bodies of Andhra Pradesh is a brackish-water lagoon?
x: Pulicat is a brackish lagoon known for birds; Kolleru is a freshwater lake between the Godavari and Krishna deltas.

s: In which district of Andhra Pradesh is the Telineelapuram bird site, known for pelicans and painted storks, located?
x: Telineelapuram, a breeding site of pelicans and painted storks, is in Srikakulam district.

s: Uppalapadu, a nesting site of painted storks and spot-billed pelicans, is in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Uppalapadu bird sanctuary lies near Guntur city; its tanks host nesting painted storks and spot-billed pelicans.

s: Kambalakonda Wildlife Sanctuary is located near which city of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Kambalakonda WLS is a dry evergreen forest in the Eastern Ghats near Visakhapatnam.

s: In which hill range of Andhra Pradesh is the Gundla Brahmeswaram Wildlife Sanctuary located?
x: Gundla Brahmeswaram WLS (1990) lies in the Nallamala hills; its northern part adjoins the Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve.

s: In which year was the Koundinya Wildlife Sanctuary, set up for elephants, established?
x: Koundinya WLS in Chittoor was set up in December 1990, after elephants moved in from Tamil Nadu's Hosur-Dharmapuri forests.

s: Krishna Wildlife Sanctuary, covering 194.81 sq km, protects the mangroves of which area?
x: Krishna WLS protects Krishna-estuary mangroves; Coringa protects the Godavari estuary.

s: Koundinya Wildlife Sanctuary in Chittoor borders which State?
x: Koundinya WLS (357.60 sq km) borders Tamil Nadu (APPSC 2018).

s: Coringa in Kakinada is known as which of the following?
x: Coringa WLS in Kakinada, with Krishna WLS, forms the Godavari-Krishna estuarine mangroves, often called India's second-largest mangrove ecosystem after the Sundarbans. By State, Gujarat has the second-largest mangrove cover. It is not an alpine, coral reef or desert ecosystem.

s: According to ISFR 2023, which State has India's second-largest mangrove cover?
x: AP calls Coringa-Krishna India's 2nd-largest mangrove ecosystem, but ISFR 2023 puts Gujarat second.

s:
Arrange the following States in decreasing order of mangrove cover:
1. Andhra Pradesh
2. Gujarat
3. West Bengal
4. Andaman and Nicobar Islands
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: West Bengal has the most mangrove cover, then Gujarat, then Andaman and Nicobar, with Andhra Pradesh least of the four.

s: Which genera are specifically associated with the mangrove vegetation of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Avicennia and Rhizophora are the mangrove genera specifically associated with the Andhra Pradesh coastal habitats.

s: What is the area of the Seshachalam Biosphere Reserve, notified in 2010?
x: Seshachalam BR covers 4,755.997 sq km; 12,454 sq km is Kachchh and 10,500 km² Gulf of Mannar.

s: Which of the following pairs relating to Sri Venkateswara National Park is wrongly matched?
o: Flora – Cycas beddomei and red sanders
Landscape – part of Sri Venkateswara Wildlife Sanctuary
x: Godavari-estuary mangroves are protected by Coringa Wildlife Sanctuary; Sri Venkateswara NP lies in the Seshachalam hills.

s: Boswellia ovalifoliolata is associated with which protected landscape?
x: Boswellia ovalifoliolata is endemic to Andhra Pradesh and is associated with the Seshachalam-Tirumala hills.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Syzygium stocksii — endemic to Andhra Pradesh
x: Cycas beddomei is endemic to Andhra Pradesh and the Eastern Ghats and occurs in the Sri Venkateswara-Seshachalam region. Syzygium stocksii is specifically identified as not being an Andhra Pradesh endemic in this context.

s: Which of the following plants is NOT endemic to Andhra Pradesh?
x: Syzygium stocksii is a Western Ghats species; Boswellia ovalifoliolata, red sanders and Cycas beddomei are endemic to AP's Eastern Ghats (Seshachalam).

s: Cycas beddomei, called a 'living fossil', is protected in which National Park of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Cycas beddomei, an Eastern Ghats endemic, grows in Sri Venkateswara NP in the Seshachalam hills.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Kolleru?
o: Its sanctuary area is about 308.55 sq km
It lies between the Godavari and Krishna deltas
x: Kolleru is a freshwater lake; the brackish lagoon of AP is Pulicat.

s: Operation Kolleru, undertaken in 2006, was associated with which action?
o: Removal of illegal fish tanks up to the plus-five-foot contour
Declaration of Kolleru as a tiger reserve
Construction of new aquaculture tanks inside the sanctuary
x: Operation Kolleru in 2006 demolished illegal fish tanks inside the sanctuary up to the +5 ft contour.

s: In which year did Kolleru Lake become a Ramsar site?
x: Kolleru has been a Ramsar site since 2002; Operation Kolleru was in 2006.

s: Which bird breeds in the Kolleru sanctuary?
x: Kolleru supports spot-billed pelican breeding and migratory waterfowl.

s: How many Ramsar sites did India have in 2026?
x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (103); it is added as option 5.
100 earlier in 2026 — now 103 (Oct 2026) (Rocket CA 2026 Part 02 p.84).
India had 103 Ramsar sites in 2026 after Sukhna Wetland (Chandigarh) and Sauj Jheel (UP) were added on 15 Oct 2026. The printed '100' was the count earlier in the year, and 64, 75 and 85 are older totals. Kolleru (AP) has been a Ramsar site since 2002.

s: Why is the Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve in the Nallamala hills significant?
o: India's oldest tiger reserve, set up under Project Tiger in 1973
India's largest tiger reserve by area
India's first Biosphere Reserve in the Eastern Ghats
India's only tiger reserve with a mangrove habitat
x: NSTR is Andhra Pradesh's only tiger reserve and India's largest tiger reserve by area. It is not a Biosphere Reserve (Seshachalam is AP's only BR), it is not the oldest reserve, and the mangrove tiger habitat is the Sundarbans.

s: Which is the only biosphere reserve of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Seshachalam (2010) is Andhra Pradesh's first and only biosphere reserve. Nallamala is a hill range, Papikonda a national park and Coringa a wildlife sanctuary.

s: What does Papikonda National Park mainly protect?
o: mangrove forests of the Krishna delta
x: Papikonda National Park protects the Papikondalu ranges situated along the Godavari River.

s: Which body runs the zoos at Visakhapatnam and Tirupati?
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
x: Indira Gandhi Zoological Park (Visakhapatnam) and Sri Venkateswara Zoological Park (Tirupati) are run by ZAAP; the CZA only recognises zoos.

s: Indira Gandhi Zoological Park, Visakhapatnam, is CZA's flagship breeding centre for which animal?
x: Indira Gandhi Zoological Park, Visakhapatnam, is the CZA's flagship dhole breeding centre.

s: Rayala, in the Anantapuramu Circle, is Andhra Pradesh's only what?
x: Rayala is AP's only elephant reserve; the only tiger reserve is NSTR and the only biosphere reserve Seshachalam.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Andhra Pradesh's protected-area network?
o: It has a Papikondalu Tiger Reserve
x: There is no 'Papikondalu Tiger Reserve'; AP's only tiger reserve is Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam.

s: Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve lies in which hill range?
x: NSTR lies in the Nallamala hills and is spread over five districts of AP and Telangana.

s: Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve ranks where among India's tiger reserves by area?
x: NSTR is AP's only tiger reserve and India's largest tiger reserve by area.

s: Over which States does the Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve spread?
x: NSTR, India's largest tiger reserve, lies in the Nallamala hills across five districts of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.

s: Which national park of Andhra Pradesh has an area of approximately 2.30 sq km and is the smallest national park in the State?
x: Rajiv Gandhi National Park, also known as Rameswaram National Park, covers approximately 2.30 sq km and is the smallest national park in Andhra Pradesh.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Rajiv Gandhi National Park — YSR Kadapa district
Sri Venkateswara National Park — Annamayya and Tirupati districts
Kasu Brahmananda Reddy National Park — present-day Andhra Pradesh
Papikonda National Park — Eluru and Alluri Sitharama Raju districts
x: Kasu Brahmananda Reddy National Park is located in Hyderabad, Telangana, not in present-day Andhra Pradesh. The other three pairs are correctly matched.

s: Where is the Kasu Brahmananda Reddy National Park located?
x: Kasu Brahmananda Reddy NP is in Hyderabad (Telangana), not in present-day AP.

s: Koundinya Wildlife Sanctuary in Chittoor district is part of which elephant reserve?
x: Koundinya is part of the Rayala Elephant Reserve, Andhra Pradesh's only elephant reserve.

s:
Arrange the following projects in chronological order of their launch:
A. Project Snow Leopard
B. Project Tiger
C. Indian Rhino Vision 2020
D. Crocodile Breeding and Management Project
x: The correct order is Project Tiger (1973), Crocodile Project (1975), Indian Rhino Vision 2020 (2005), and Project Snow Leopard (2009).

s: Which species is covered by one of the five new national projects added by MoEFCC?
x: The five additions were dolphin, Asian elephant, gharial, Great Indian Bustard and Olive Ridley turtle; snow leopard was not among them.

s: Which one of the following was the first tiger reserve under Project Tiger?
x: Corbett was the first tiger reserve under Project Tiger, formally included on 1 April 1973.

s: From which body do projects located in tiger corridors require clearance?
o: Standing Committee of the National Board for Wildlife
x: Projects in tiger corridors require clearance from the Standing Committee of the National Board for Wildlife.

s: Project Tiger began in 1973 with how many tiger reserves?
x: Project Tiger started in 1973 with 9 reserves covering 18,278 sq km; today there are 58 reserves.

s: Which of the following was among the first nine tiger reserves under Project Tiger?
x: Palamau was among the first nine reserves of Project Tiger, which was launched on the advice of Indira Gandhi's task force.

s: A railway line through which tiger corridor has been reported as a conservation concern?
x: A railway line through the Satpura-Melghat corridor is a reported concern, alongside tiger dispersal and rising conflict.

s: Which is the largest tiger reserve in India by area?
x: Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve (NSTR) in the Nallamala hills of Andhra Pradesh is India's largest tiger reserve, with a core area of about 5,443 sq km. Bandipur, Corbett and Kanha are smaller.

s: Which became India's 58th tiger reserve in March 2025?
x: Madhav TR (MP) is the 58th and newest; Ratapani was the 57th (Dec 2024).

s: Which period did the Action Plan for Vulture Conservation, calling for State-level vulture committees and more breeding centres, cover?
x: The 2020–25 Action Plan called for State-level committees and more breeding centres; its extension to 2030 came later.

s: Where is India's first vulture breeding centre, the Jatayu Conservation Breeding Centre, located?
x: The Vulture Conservation and Breeding Centre is at Pinjore, Haryana. Keoladeo is where the decline was first noticed (1998), Jaisalmer hosts the GIB breeding centres, and Darjeeling breeds red pandas.

s:
Which of the following veterinary drugs were banned for animal use in 2023?
1. Aceclofenac
2. Ketoprofen
3. Diclofenac
x: Aceclofenac and ketoprofen were banned for animal use in 2023; diclofenac had already been banned in 2006.

s: In which year was the decline of vultures in India first noticed at Keoladeo?
x: The decline was noticed at Keoladeo in 1998; 2006 is when veterinary diclofenac was banned.

s: How does diclofenac in cattle carcasses mainly kill vultures?
x: Diclofenac causes kidney failure (visceral gout) in vultures, which explains their decline; meloxicam is the safe alternative.

s: What is the full form of SAVE in vulture conservation?
x: SAVE is the Saving Asia's Vultures from Extinction consortium.

s: How many of India's nine vulture species are Critically Endangered?
x: Four of the nine are CR: white-rumped, slender-billed, long-billed and red-headed vultures.

s: Which veterinary drug is the safe alternative to diclofenac for vultures?
x: Meloxicam is safe for vultures; diclofenac (2006) and aceclofenac and ketoprofen (2023) were banned for animal use.

s: In which State did the world's first release of captive-bred slender-billed vultures take place in August 2026?
x: Five captive-bred slender-billed vultures were released from the BNHS centre in Assam, a world first.

s: Which animals does Project Dolphin cover?
o: Riverine and marine dolphins and other cetaceans
x: Project Dolphin covers both riverine and marine dolphins as well as other cetaceans.

s: In which Schedule of the Wildlife (Protection) Act is the Ganges River Dolphin included?
x: The Ganges River Dolphin is listed in Schedule I of the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972.

s: How many dolphins did the first national assessment of riverine dolphins record?
x: The first national assessment recorded 6,327 riverine dolphins. The survey covered 8,500 km across 28 rivers in eight States; 8,500 is therefore a distance, not the dolphin count.

s: Where is the National Dolphin Research Centre located?
x: The National Dolphin Research Centre is at Patna; Vikramshila Gangetic Dolphin Sanctuary is at Bhagalpur.

s: Which one of the following is NOT a recognised threat to the Ganges River Dolphin?
x: Pollution, entanglement or bycatch in fishing nets, dams and barrages, poaching, killing for oil and boat traffic are recognised threats. Expansion of desert grasslands is not identified as a threat to the river dolphin.

s: On which date is National Dolphin Day observed?
x: 5 October, the date in 2009 the Ganges River Dolphin became the National Aquatic Animal, is National Dolphin Day.

s: Where is the Vikramshila Gangetic Dolphin Sanctuary located?
x: Vikramshila Sanctuary is at Bhagalpur, Bihar; the National Dolphin Research Centre is at Patna.

s: In which year was the Ganges River Dolphin declared the National Aquatic Animal of India?
x: The Ganges River Dolphin was declared India's National Aquatic Animal on 5 October 2009; 5 October is now National Dolphin Day.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Ganges River Dolphin:
1. It was declared the National Aquatic Animal of India in 2009.
2. It is listed as Vulnerable in the IUCN Red List.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: It became the National Aquatic Animal in 2009, but its IUCN status is Endangered, not Vulnerable.

s: The Ganges River Dolphin is found in which group of countries?
x: It lives in the Ganga-Brahmaputra-Meghna and Karnaphuli-Sangu systems of India, Nepal and Bangladesh.

s: In which year was Indian Rhino Vision 2020 for the one-horned rhinoceros in Assam launched?
x: Indian Rhino Vision 2020 began in 2005; Project Lion and Project Dolphin began in 2020.

s: In which year was the Crocodile Breeding and Management Project, supported by FAO-UNDP, launched?
x: The Crocodile Breeding and Management Project began in 1975 for gharial, mugger and saltwater crocodile.

s: In which year was Project Snow Leopard launched?
x: Project Snow Leopard dates from 2009; Project Lion and Project Dolphin are both 2020.

s: What is the IUCN Red List status of the Great Indian Bustard?
x: The GIB is Critically Endangered, with fewer than 150 birds left in the wild.

s: The principal natural range of the Great Indian Bustard is associated with which of the following regions?
x: The Great Indian Bustard is found mainly in the Thar region of Rajasthan, although its range also extends into parts of Gujarat, Maharashtra and Karnataka.

s: What is the major conservation threat to the Great Indian Bustard in solar and wind-energy zones?
x: Collisions with overhead power lines are a major threat to the Great Indian Bustard, particularly in solar and wind-energy zones.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about M.K. Ranjitsinh v. Union of India?
o: In March 2024, the 2021 blanket direction was upheld without change
In 2021, the Supreme Court directed that power lines in GIB habitat be laid underground
In March 2024, an expert committee was constituted
It concerned protection of the Great Indian Bustard from power-line impacts
x: In March 2024 the blanket undergrounding direction was modified, not upheld unchanged, and an expert committee was set up.

s: In the context of the Supreme Court’s March 2024 proceedings concerning the Great Indian Bustard, which constitutional rights were recognised in relation to adverse effects of climate change?
x: The Supreme Court recognised a right against the adverse effects of climate change under Articles 14 and 21.

s: What is the zoological name of the Great Indian Bustard?
x: The Great Indian Bustard (Godawan) is Ardeotis nigriceps; Platanista gangetica is the Ganges River Dolphin.

s: Where is conservation breeding of the Great Indian Bustard carried out?
x: GIB breeding is at Sam and Ramdevra, Jaisalmer; Pinjore breeds vultures.

s: Which States share the National Chambal Sanctuary, India's only tri-state riverine protected area?
o: Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh
Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Madhya Pradesh
x: The National Chambal Sanctuary (1979) spans Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh along the Chambal river. Gujarat, Bihar and Haryana are not part of it.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the whale shark?
o: The Gujarat coast is an important seasonal location for it.
It can reach about 50 feet in length.
Gujarat's whale shark protection programme started in 2006.
x: Gujarat's whale shark protection programme began in 2004, not 2006.

s: The Kharai Camel can survive in which of the following ecosystems?
x: The Kharai camel of Kutch survives in both coastal and dry ecosystems, swimming to mangrove islands to feed. It is not found in alpine, glacial or forest habitats.
