s: The snow leopard was declared the national symbol of which country in December 2023?
x: Kyrgyzstan made the snow leopard its national symbol in December 2023; the cat has 12 range countries including India.

s: Where was the crocodile sub-project for the saltwater crocodile (Baula) set up?
x: The Baula (saltwater crocodile) sub-project was at Dangamal in Bhitarkanika, Odisha; the mugger sub-project was at Ramatirtha.

s: Which place in Nagaland is called the 'Falcon Capital of the World'?
x: Pangti, near the Doyang reservoir where Amur falcons gather in huge numbers, is the 'Falcon Capital of the World'.

s:
Assertion (A): CMS COP13 was held at Gandhinagar, Gujarat, in February 2020.
Reason (R): The COP13 mascot 'Gibi' represented the Amur falcon.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: COP13 was at Gandhinagar in February 2020, but 'Gibi' represented the Great Indian Bustard, not the Amur falcon.

s: Which Indian species was NOT among those added to CMS Appendix I at COP13?
x: India's Asian elephant, GIB and Bengal florican were added to Appendix I at COP13.

s: Where was the 14th Conference of Parties of the CMS (February 2024) held?
x: COP14 was at Samarkand, Uzbekistan (Feb 2024); COP13 was at Gandhinagar (2020).

s: At which place in Nagaland do Amur falcons make their stopover?
x: Amur falcons stop over at the Doyang reservoir, Nagaland, before crossing the Arabian Sea.

s: Project Elephant was launched as a Centrally Sponsored Scheme in which month and year?
x: Project Elephant was launched in February 1992 as a Centrally Sponsored Scheme (some sources say 1991-92). '1990' is the trap: APPSC 2022 treated a 1990 launch as the incorrect statement.

s: In which year was the elephant declared India's National Heritage Animal?
x: The elephant was declared the National Heritage Animal in 2010. 1992 is the launch of Project Elephant, 2009 is when the Ganges river dolphin became the National Aquatic Animal, and 2020 is the launch of Project Lion and Project Dolphin.

s: Rayala in Andhra Pradesh is the State's only what?
x: Rayala is Andhra Pradesh's only elephant reserve; the State also has India's largest tiger reserve.

s: What is the full form of MIKE, associated with elephant conservation?
o: Monitoring the Illegal Killing of Elephants
x: MIKE stands for Monitoring the Illegal Killing of Elephants and is a CITES programme.

s: What is the gestation period of the Asian elephant, the longest of any mammal?
x: Asian elephant gestation is about 22 months, the longest among mammals.

s: India has how many Elephant Reserves?
x: India has 33 Elephant Reserves in 14 States.

s: India holds about what share of the world's Asian elephants?
x: India has about 60% of Asian elephants, with a population of 22,446 (Apr 2026).

s: What are tuskless male Asian elephants called?
x: Only male Asian elephants have tusks; tuskless males are called makhnas.

s: What was the estimated population of Asian elephants in India in April 2026?
x: India's elephant population was 22,446 (Apr 2026); India has about 60% of the world's Asian elephants.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Project Elephant began in 1992. Project Tiger began in 1973 (not 2010), the NGT was set up in 2010 (not 1992), and the NTCA was set up in 2006 (not 1973).

s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the seven big cats covered by the International Big Cat Alliance?
x: The seven big cats are tiger, lion, leopard, snow leopard, cheetah, jaguar and puma. Gharial is not a big cat covered by the IBCA.

s: Which one of the following pairs of species and recent population figure is correctly matched?
x: The reported figures were 891 Asiatic lions and 718 snow leopards. Assam had 2,650 rhinos in 2018, while the overall rhino population was over 4,000.

s: Which cheetahs have been introduced in India under Project Cheetah?
o: Asiatic cheetahs bred in captivity in India
x: The introduced animals are African cheetahs; the critically endangered Asiatic cheetah survives only in Iran.

s: In which year was the cheetah, the only large mammal to go extinct in India in recent history, declared extinct in India?
x: The cheetah was declared extinct in India in 1952. 1947 is Independence, 1972 is the Wildlife (Protection) Act, and 2012 is when the Supreme Court first ruled on its reintroduction.

s: The International Big Cat Alliance was launched in April 2023 to mark which occasion?
o: the declaration of the cheetah as extinct in India
the first census of Asiatic lions
x: The International Big Cat Alliance was launched in April 2023 to mark 50 years of Project Tiger.

s: Which of the following Project Cheetah batches is correctly matched with its source?
x: Two females came from Botswana in May 2026. Eight cheetahs came from Namibia in September 2022 and twelve from South Africa in February 2023.

s: Where is the Secretariat of the International Big Cat Alliance located?
x: IBCA, a treaty-based inter-governmental body, has its Secretariat in New Delhi; Geneva is not its headquarters.

s: Barda Wildlife Sanctuary has been proposed as a second home for Asiatic lions. What is the main criticism of this proposal?
o: Is too close to Gir to provide a genuine metapopulation safeguard
Has no forest cover at all
Is exclusively a marine protected area
x: Critics argue that Barda Wildlife Sanctuary is too close to Gir to function as an effective separate metapopulation safeguard.

s: Which is the second site of Project Cheetah, to which two males were moved from Kuno in April 2025?
x: Gandhi Sagar WLS (Mandsaur, MP) received two males from Kuno on 20 April 2025.

s: In which country does the Asiatic cheetah now survive?
x: The Asiatic cheetah survives only in Iran, so India brought African cheetahs.

s:
Consider the following statements about the International Big Cat Alliance:
1. It was launched at Mysuru.
2. It covers seven big cats, including the jaguar and puma.
3. Its Secretariat is at Geneva.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: IBCA was launched at Mysuru and covers seven big cats; its Secretariat is in New Delhi, not Geneva.

s: Kuno was initially selected as a second home for which animal before being used for Project Cheetah?
o: Gharials from the National Chambal Sanctuary
x: Kuno was initially chosen as a second home for Gir's Asiatic lions. The Supreme Court ordered lion translocation in 2013, but Gujarat did not implement it.

s: How many range countries is the International Big Cat Alliance open to?
x: The IBCA is open to 96 range countries of the seven big cats and also to non-range countries; it has 27 members.

s:
Consider the following statements about the International Big Cat Alliance:
1. Membership is open only to range countries of big cats.
2. The Union Cabinet approved Rs 150 crore for it for five years.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Non-range countries can also join the IBCA, so statement 1 is wrong; the Cabinet approved Rs 150 crore for 2023-24 to 2027-28.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: NTCA is chaired by the Union Environment Minister and became statutory through the 2006 WPA amendment; the PM chairs the NBWL.

s: The All India Tiger Estimation is conducted at what interval and jointly by which organisations?
o: Every five years by MoEFCC and BNHS
Every three years by WII and Forest Survey of India
Every four years by NTCA and WII
Every two years by NTCA and Zoological Survey of India
x: All India Tiger Estimation is conducted every four years by NTCA and the Wildlife Institute of India.

s: Which of the following correctly describes the fifth cycle of All India Tiger Estimation conducted in 2022?
o: 3,925 tigers, with an upper estimate of 3,682
3,682 tigers, with an upper estimate of 3,925
2,967 tigers, with an upper estimate of 3,682
3,682 tigers, with an upper estimate of 4,925
x: The 2022 estimation recorded 3,682 tigers, with an upper estimate of 3,925.

s: India holds approximately what share of the world’s wild tiger population?
x: India holds approximately 70–75% of the world’s wild tigers.

s: Which technique replaced the old pugmark method in all-India tiger estimation?
o: Camera trapping supported by ExtractCompare software
Counting tiger kills reported by villages
Only satellite imagery without field verification
x: The old pugmark technique was replaced by camera trapping and ExtractCompare software, which identifies tigers through stripe patterns.

s: Where is the headquarters of the Global Tiger Forum, set up in 1993?
x: The Global Tiger Forum is in New Delhi; IUCN and WWF are at Gland.

s: On which date is International Tiger Day, begun by the 2010 Global Tiger Summit, observed?
x: The St Petersburg Summit (Nov 2010) began International Tiger Day on 29 July.

s: What is the full form of M-STrIPES used in tiger reserves?
o: Monitoring Scheme for Tigers - Indian Population Estimation Study
Mapping System for Tiger Ranges - Intensive Patrol and Evaluation Scheme
Monitoring System for Tigers - Intensive Protection and Ecological Status
Management System for Tiger Reserves - Integrated Patrol and Estimation Survey
x: M-STrIPES (Monitoring System for Tigers - Intensive Protection and Ecological Status) is NTCA-WII software launched in 2010.

s: Which State had the highest number of tigers in the 2022 All India Tiger Estimation?
x: Madhya Pradesh had 785 tigers in 2022, ahead of Karnataka (563), Uttarakhand (560) and Maharashtra (444).

s: What was the goal of TX2, adopted at the 2010 Global Tiger Summit in St Petersburg?
o: To double the number of wild tigers by 2022
To create 20 new tiger reserves by 2020
To ban the trade in tiger parts by 2015
To translocate tigers to all range countries
x: TX2 aimed to double wild tiger numbers by 2022, a goal India met early.

s: In the Management Effectiveness Evaluation (MEE) 2022, how many of the 51 tiger reserves assessed were rated 'Excellent'?
x: MEE 2022 assessed 51 tiger reserves; 12 were 'Excellent' and the average score was 78%.

s: What is the full form of CA|TS, an accreditation given to tiger reserves?
x: CA|TS = Conservation Assured | Tiger Standards, a set of criteria to check whether a site's management will conserve tigers.

s: How many Indian tiger reserves received CA|TS accreditation on International Tiger Day 2021?
x: On 29 July 2021, 14 Indian tiger reserves (e.g. Kaziranga, Manas, Kanha, Panna) got CA|TS accreditation.

s: The Great hornbill is the logo of which organisation?
o: International Union for Conservation of Nature
x: The Great hornbill is the logo of the Bombay Natural History Society (BNHS).

s: What is the main aim of Project HANUMAN, launched by Andhra Pradesh on World Wildlife Day?
o: Restore coral reefs along the coast
Increase tiger numbers through captive breeding
x: Andhra Pradesh launched Project HANUMAN on 3 March 2026, World Wildlife Day, to reduce human-wildlife conflict.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Species Recovery Programme under CSS-Integrated Development of Wildlife Habitats?
o: The Great Indian Bustard and marine turtles are among the species it covers
Hangul and dugong are among the species it covers
Gharial and sloth bear have been covered by it from the start
x: Gharial and sloth bear were only recommended for inclusion (June 2026); they were not covered from the start.

s: For how long was the Recovery Programme for Critically Endangered Species, funded through the National CAMPA Advisory Council, initially sanctioned?
x: The programme was sanctioned for an initial period of five years.

s: Where is the headquarters of the Wildlife Institute of India located?
x: The Wildlife Institute of India (WII) is headquartered at Dehradun.

s: Where is the Wildlife Trust of India (WTI) headquartered?
x: WTI is at Noida, Uttar Pradesh; BNHS is at Mumbai and IUCN and WWF at Gland, Switzerland.

s: Which animal is the logo of WWF?
x: WWF's logo is the giant panda; the great hornbill is BNHS's logo.

s: Where is the headquarters of IUCN?
x: IUCN (1948) and WWF are headquartered at Gland, Switzerland.

s: Where is the headquarters of the Bombay Natural History Society (BNHS)?
x: BNHS, founded in 1883 with the great hornbill as its logo, is headquartered in Mumbai.

s: In which year was the Bombay Natural History Society founded?
x: BNHS dates from 1883; IUCN is 1948, WWF 1961 and WII 1982.
